headline: Chip Rout Casts a Shadow Over Monday's Open as Gulf Tensions Simmer
body_html:
US stocks head into Monday's session with a cautious tone. Asian shares fell overnight as investors waited on a major chip designer's earnings, while a high-profile AI listing put the recent tech rally to the test. Oil edged higher on shipping worries in the Strait of Hormuz.

Friday's session ended evenly split beneath the surface: 335 stocks rose and 324 fell among the 666 we track. The semiconductor group did the damage, sliding 3.6%. Financials lost 1.35% and materials 0.79%. Consumer shares gained 0.96% and energy added 0.87%. AMD dropped 8.75%, while Modine Manufacturing surged 27.86% to lead the winners.

At the open, watch whether chip stocks steady or extend their losses ahead of that earnings report. Also watch oil and Gulf-linked trading as Houthi missile claims and Iran-related strikes keep the region on edge, and any news on a US-Iran deal. Pre-market prices are thin and unreliable, so the first hour's follow-through matters more than early moves.

briefs.headline: Chip stocks take Friday's heaviest hit
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 3.6% on Friday, the weakest group in our universe. AMD slid 8.75%, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor lost 10.91% and PDF Solutions dropped 9.01%. Traders will look to the open for signs of stabilization ahead of a major rival's earnings.

briefs.headline: Modine and Stantec lead a lopsided winners' list
briefs.body: Modine Manufacturing jumped 27.86% on Friday, the biggest gain we tracked. Engineering firm Stantec rose 14.06%. Their moves helped industrials finish up 0.37% even as the broader market stayed evenly divided between gainers and losers.

briefs.headline: Hormuz tanker incidents keep oil bid
briefs.body: Crude edged higher as tanker incidents near the Strait of Hormuz renewed concerns about shipping safety. Energy shares were already among Friday's better performers, up 0.87%. Any further disruption reports could set the tone for the sector at the open.

briefs.headline: Gulf markets slide on missile claims
briefs.body: Gulf bourses fell as Yemen's Houthis said they fired ballistic missiles toward Riyadh, and reports said Iran struck Bahrain. Anti-Houthi forces were also reported retreating in Yemen. The escalation adds a risk premium that could spill into energy and global sentiment.

briefs.headline: US-Iran deal doubts hang over India's rupee and bonds
briefs.body: Uncertainty over a possible US-Iran agreement is expected to weigh on India's rupee and government bonds. Investors are also weighing the likely interest-rate paths of the Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of India, which could shape overnight flows.

briefs.headline: UK asking prices fall more than usual
briefs.body: Rightmove reported that UK property asking prices fell in November by more than the seasonal norm. The drop points to a cooling housing market heading into winter. Homebuilders were modestly higher in our universe on Friday, up 0.47%.
